content: In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using streptomycin injection, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (such as tobramycin or gentamicin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Streptomycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as BCG or typhoid vaccines). Notify your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Avoid becoming pregnant while using streptomycin, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has instructed you to take low doses of aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81–162 milligrams daily), continue taking the aspirin as directed. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, laboratory and medical tests (such as kidney function, hearing tests, and streptomycin blood levels) should be performed regularly. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive the medication as soon as possible. Store unmixed medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Streptomycin can sometimes cause serious nerve damage, potentially leading to permanent hearing loss and balance problems. The risk is higher if you have kidney disease, are receiving high doses, use the drug for a prolonged period, are older than 60 years, or become severely dehydrated. To reduce the risk of dehydration, drink plenty of fluids unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Your doctor will monitor your progress to minimize these risks and may test your hearing, kidney function, and streptomycin blood levels. Before undergoing surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using this medication. Streptomycin is used in combination with other medications to treat active tuberculosis (TB) infections when other TB drugs cannot be used or when the TB strain is drug-resistant. It belongs to a class of drugs known as aminoglycoside antibiotics. This medication is administered by injection, usually into a muscle, as directed by your doctor. When starting TB treatment, it is typically given once daily or as instructed. Rotate the injection site daily to prevent skin irritation. The dosage is based on the type of infection, your weight, medical condition, streptomycin blood levels, and response to treatment. If you are administering this medication at home, learn all preparation and usage instructions from your healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. TB treatment with this medication usually lasts for nine months or longer. After one to two months of daily streptomycin injections, your doctor may reduce the frequency to two or three times per week. Your doctor may also instruct you to stop using streptomycin before discontinuing other TB medications. Do not stop taking this medication (or other TB antibiotics) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time, as this may worsen side effects or make the infection more difficult to treat. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or loss of appetite. Pain, irritation, or redness may occur at the injection site. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects.
